title: *Mali: Climate Resilience and Environmental Governance*
temporal_coverage: Historical climate through 2023; policy context to 2025
methodology: Literature/data synthesis using a nexus framework; expert review
limitations: Synthesis, not causal evaluation; some climate-conflict wording stronger than underlying evidence warrants. (World Bank)

title: *Mali Economic Update - Special Chapter: Strengthening Financial Resilience of Pastoralists to Drought*
methodology: Six climate-model/emissions combinations linked to biophysical/economic modelling; drought analysis
limitations: Future precipitation highly uncertain; economic model is scenario-based. (World Bank)

title: *Contribution Déterminée au Niveau National révisée*
limitations: UNFCCC PDF is ~20 MB and could not be rendered by the browser interface; the direct file was successfully retrieved separately. Section §6.2 was cross-checked against the public FAOLEX mirror. Exact PDF page for §6.2: LOCATOR NOT VERIFIED. (UNFCCC)

title: *Agence de l’Environnement et du Développement Durable: session du Comité de coordination et suivi de mise en œuvre de la CDN*
limitations: Describes process and commitments, not independently evaluated implementation outcomes. (Government of Mali)

title: *Climate-related Security Risks and Peacebuilding in Mali*
geographic_coverage: Mali, with emphasis on north/centre and MINUSMA
methodology: Qualitative process tracing; literature/UN documents; 57 interviews/correspondence
limitations: Single case/plausibility probe; interview perspectives; written before MINUSMA withdrawal and subsequent conflict changes. (SIPRI)

title: *Is climate exacerbating the root causes of conflict in Mali? A climate security analysis through a structural equation modeling approach*
organization: Frontiers in Climate / Alliance Bioversity-CIAT authors
geographic_coverage: National household sample merged at cercle level
limitations: Observational model; one specified food-production pathway; associations should not be read as proof of event-level causality. (Frontiers)

title: *Mali Humanitarian Situation Report No. 1*
methodology: Cluster/government/UN reporting and UNICEF programme monitoring
limitations: Humanitarian estimates can be revised; UNICEF outputs are not independent impact evaluation. (UNICEF)

title: *Situation report on the crisis in Mali - April 2026*
geographic_coverage: Bamako, Gao, Mopti, Kidal and affected IDP sites
limitations: Short-period operational source; response counts are outputs, not effectiveness estimates. (United Nations Population Fund)

title: *Mali - Operational Data Portal*
limitations: Different population series have different update dates; registered, preregistered and unregistered refugees must not be conflated. (UNHCR Data Portal)

title: *Humanitarian aid cuts push millions deeper into hunger amid rising violence and population displacement in West and Central Africa*
methodology: Cadre Harmonisé and WFP operational evidence
limitations: WFP is an implementing agency; ration comparison is not presented as a randomized impact evaluation. (World Food Programme)

title: *GIEWS Country Brief: Mali*
methodology: Cadre Harmonisé, production/price monitoring and seasonal forecasts
limitations: Older than 2026 humanitarian sources; seasonal forecasts are prospective and conflict remains a major confounder. (FAOHome)

title: *Impacts of Development Aid to Mali 2008-2021: A Systematic Review of Evaluation Reports - Part I*
organization: Netherlands Ministry of Foreign Affairs, IOB-commissioned research
methodology: 6,296 title/abstract screens; 588 full texts; 104 Mali studies included; methodological quality thresholds
limitations: Evidence ends in 2021; country-level evaluations were included by default without the same quality threshold.

title: *Mali Community Resilience and Inclusive Services Project - Malidenko (P505025), Project Appraisal Document*
methodology: Project appraisal, institutional and fiduciary design
limitations: Design evidence only: committees, facilitators and grievance systems are intended mechanisms, not proven outcomes. (World Bank)
